title: [Peek] Minimum window size is defined inconsistently in XAML and code
author: daverayment

status.label: Owned by the reporting collaborator
status.detail: The exact conflicting minimum-size definitions are identified and the collaborator who filed the issue is assigned.

next_action.label: Leave with the assignee
next_action.reason: Avoid duplicating an implementation-scoped issue with established ownership.

judgment.rationale: This is an implementation-scoped report authored and assigned to a PowerToys collaborator, with the relevant files and unit mismatch already identified.
evidence: Peek.UI/PeekXAML/MainWindow.xaml declares 480 by 320 minimum dimensions in DIPs.
Peek.Common/Constants/WindowConstants.cs declares 500 by 500 values that runtime sizing divides by monitor scale.
The issue is assigned to its collaborator author and cross-references the companion scaled-image issue 50244.
judgment.recommended_action: Leave implementation and validation with the current assignee; do not create a parallel dashboard design.

issue_context.summary: Peek enforces different minimum window dimensions in XAML and runtime sizing logic, using different units on scaled displays.
known_information: The report is against current main and provides exact XAML and C# values.
A 512 by 512 image on a 175% display produces a disproportionately wide window.
The collaborator author is assigned to the issue.
inferences: Unifying the minimum-size source and unit conversion should remove code-path-dependent sizing, but the final implementation remains the assignee's responsibility.
issue_context.analysis: The issue is already at implementation scope rather than discovery scope. Current source confirms the two definitions, and explicit collaborator assignment makes independent design work duplicative.
initial_investigation: Verified the issue's assignment and its relationship to issue 50244.
